title: Myth vs Reality: was it about states' rights?

segments.text: Myth: the Civil War was about states' rights.
Reality: the Confederacy said it was about slavery.
Mississippi's declaration says its position is thoroughly identified with the institution of slavery.
Texas, Georgia and South Carolina said the same.
The Confederate constitution itself protected the right to own enslaved people.
And Confederate vice president Alexander Stephens called slavery the cornerstone of the new government.
Even the right the South defended was the right to hold people as property.
Lincoln said it plainly in his second inaugural address:
all knew this interest was, somehow, the cause of the war.
Slavery was the cause. Union was the stake.
Emancipation made it the war's purpose.

verify: Mississippi declaration quote; Stephens 'Cornerstone Speech' 21 Mar 1861; TX/GA/SC declarations cite slavery
Confederate constitution protects slavery (Art. I s.9(4)); Lincoln Second Inaugural 4 Mar 1865: 'All knew that this interest was, somehow, the cause of the war'
